stance.label: Taiwan in a bear market, risk rising; stick to the plan

headline: Taiwan stocks plunge 1,768 points through the bear-market line; foreigners keep selling, NT$ breaks 33
summary: Taiwan stocks are now in a bear market by definition, but not one driven by the economy or credit. The index fell 4.4% and is −22.9% from its high, yet only 2 systemic lights are on; the likeliest third is a sharp NT dollar drop. Tonight, watch US jobless claims and Walmart earnings. Keep regular investing on plan.

watch.label: TAIEX bear-market line (−20% from high)
watch.note: Closed 38,426.89 on 11/19; needs a 3.7% gain to get back above, then 5 closes above the 200-day line to return to a correction

watch.label: S&P 500 200-day line
watch.note: 2 closes below, 0.3% away; 5 closes below with a flat line would mean weak

overview.lead: Taiwan broke its bear-market line as foreign selling, rates and AI valuations hit at once: large and small caps fell together, with nowhere to hide.
points: The TAIEX fell 1,768 points to 38,427, through the bear-market line.
It is −22.9% from the 10/6 high, a bear market by definition.
1,203 listed stocks fell and only 132 rose.
TSMC (2330) fell 3.45% and MediaTek (2454) 5.6%, leading the sell-off.
The OTC index fell more than 6% intraday; small caps fell harder than the main board.

focus.lead: None of the nine tracked names hit a new tier today; the four Taiwan-linked ones took the hardest hit, and fund NAVs do not yet show today's plunge.
points: 0050 fell 4.1% and is −22.6% from its high, a new low for this drop.
0050's fifth tier is 81.55, 9.6% away.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) and Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) share 6 top-ten names worth about 27%; their next NAVs will fall together.
Both Taiwan fund NAVs only run to 11/18 and miss today's TSMC and MediaTek drops.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV only runs to 11/17 and misses both days of Taiwan losses.
QQQ's third tier is 2.1% away, still the closest tier among the nine.

position.lead: No new tier hit today; 0050 set a new low for this drop but is still nearly 10% from its fifth tier.
points: 0050 fifth tier 81.55, 9.6% away.
QQQ third tier 645.71, 2.1% away.
SPY second tier 701.18, 4.0% away.
AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) second tier 85.08, 4.1% away (11/18 NAV).
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) fifth tier 1,218.74, 7.6% away (11/18 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used every tier; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: The outside pressure is still rates: hike bets keep the US dollar firm, the NT dollar hit an 18-month low, and outflows have not stopped.
points: The NT dollar fell to 33.02 intraday, an 18-month low.
USD/TWD was 32.91 on 11/18, down 0.43 in a month.
Waller said December may need a 50 bp hike, or 25 bp with more to follow.
The 2-year Treasury yield is 4.80%; the 10-year is 5.07%.
High-yield spreads are 3.43% (11/17), far from the 5% warning line.

sentiment.lead: Taiwan's panic-bottom signals now show 4 lights, missing only extreme foreign selling; a bottom is closer but not confirmed.
points: The TAIEX RSI is 30, oversold.
Only 14% of listed stocks are above the 200-day line and 8% above the 50-day line.
2 new highs versus 329 new lows; the washout is near extreme.
Foreign 20-day selling is about NT$1.08 trillion, still below this site's extreme threshold.
CNN's Fear & Greed Index is 24.6, still extreme fear.

sectors.lead: No safe haven today: every sector fell, and the AI supply chain that bounced yesterday fell hardest.
points: Optoelectronics fell 9% and electronic components 8.3%.
Auras (3017) hit limit-down and ASE Technology (3711) fell 8%, giving back yesterday's rebound.
Cathay Financial (2882) fell 5.9%; financials were sold for a 2nd day.
Electronic components are down 39% in a month, the core of this decline.
Construction, food and defensive names like Chunghwa Telecom (2412) held up best.

taiwan.lead: Foreign selling shrank but did not stop, and dealer hedging was today's heaviest seller; futures shorts stay high, so flows have not improved.
points: Foreign investors sold NT$24.3B, about NT$180.3B over a week.
Foreigners have now sold for 4 straight days; the selling has not stopped.
Dealers sold NT$23.3B, including NT$21.4B of hedging.
Investment trusts bought only NT$1.5B, weaker support than the day before.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures are 99,219 contracts, up only 354 in a week.
Margin loans are NT$508B (11/18), down about a fifth in 20 days; deleveraging continues.

watch.lead: Tonight, watch US jobless claims, Walmart earnings and the Anthropic listing; tomorrow, see whether the short-selling curbs ease the selling.
points: The TAIEX must get back above 39,858 to leave bear-market territory.
US initial jobless claims come out at 21:30 Taipei, a check on the economy light.
Walmart (WMT) reports before the US open on 11/19, a read on US consumers.
Anthropic lists as ANT on 11/19 (US time), priced at US$83; watch whether it pulls money from AI leaders.
Short-selling curbs start 11/20: stocks closing down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted below the prior close the next day.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is in a "bear market (down ≥ 20%)" of the "risk rising" kind; one more systemic light would make it a downtrend. US stocks are still a pullback.
points: Trend: the TAIEX is 7.4% below its 200-day line, with 4 closes below.
The 200-day line is still rising 3.4%; even a 5th close below tomorrow will not trigger the defense rule unless the line flattens.
Systemic lights: 2 on (US below its 200-day line, Taiwan breadth collapse); credit, the economy and financial conditions are still fine.
Closest to turning on is the NT dollar light: it fell to 33.02 intraday, an 18-month low.
Panic-bottom signals: 4 on (oversold, margin deleveraging, breadth washout, surging new lows), missing only extreme foreign selling.
History: all 9 past drops to this level went past −20%, and 4 went past −30%.
But nearly 90% of those 9 were higher a year later, with a median of +18.8%.
Only 1 fell this fast; the sample is too small, for reference only.
What would change the call: a close back above 39,858, then 5 closes above the 200-day line, returns it to a correction.
3 systemic lights would mean a downtrend driven by the economy or credit; the S&P 500 is only 0.3% under its 200-day line and still a pullback.

news.read: Foreigners have sold 4 days in a row, but 20-day selling is still below this site's extreme threshold, the one missing panic-bottom light.

news.title: Foreign selling pushed the NT dollar to 33.02 intraday, an 18-month low
news.read: A sharp NT dollar drop is the likeliest third systemic light for Taiwan; the exchange rate is the number to watch.

news.title: The OTC index fell more than 6% intraday; 64 listed and 82 OTC stocks hit limit-down (intraday)
news.read: Small caps fell harder than the main board; the breadth washout is near extreme, one of the panic-bottom signals.

news.title: The FSC announced short-selling curbs after the close: from 11/20, stocks closing down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted below the prior close the next day
news.read: Curbs can slow forced selling but do not change the direction of foreign selling; watch whether selling eases tomorrow.

news.title: Waller said December may need a 50 bp hike, or 25 bp with a signal for another in January
news.read: Hike bets keep the US dollar firm and weigh on growth valuations, the outside reason behind foreign selling and the weak NT dollar.

news.title: Anthropic priced its IPO at US$83 a share, above the US$70–78 range, and lists as ANT on 11/19 (US time)
news.read: Tonight's debut is a gauge of AI appetite; a new listing can also pull money from existing AI leaders.
